subject: Streaming chat temporal backfill & elevated latency — immediate mitigations and follow-up
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.ai>
To: Shelby Cho <shelby@veloxai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Streaming chat temporal backfill & elevated latency — immediate mitigations and follow-up

Hi Shelby —

Thanks for flagging the issues you saw this morning. We detected elevated token emission latency on the streaming/chat endpoints that affected a subset of VeloxAI sessions between ~08:40–09:05 PST. Symptoms we saw: intermittent long pauses during streams, out-of-order "catch-up" tokens (what you described as "gaps then a burst"), and longer tail latencies for sessions with many short interactions.

What we did immediately:
- Scoped affected population to us-west cluster handling VeloxAI production routing.
- Enabled a temporary model-variant fallback for sessions hitting the slow path to provide a steady, lower-latency emit cadence.
- Deployed a conservative prefix-KV caching policy to reduce repeated computation on the common prefixes you use.
- Collected end-to-end traces and client-side metrics into the attached telemetry bundle.

Short-term asks for you:
- If you can, please reproduce a small failing session and send the trace id from the client logs (X-Session-Trace header) — that will help map to our traces.
- Try disabling any very-short-timeout retry logic on your side for ~2 hours; retries can amplify backpressure during a rolling mitigation.

We're treating this as high priority. Marissa and Laura are leading the remediation. We'll continue to update you in this thread and follow with a short post-incident summary.

Attachments included: veloxai_incident-telemetry.zip (client+server traces), mitigation-checklist.pdf (temporary config suggestions).

Apologies for the disruption — we know steady streaming is critical for your product.

— Logan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: Streaming chat temporal backfill & elevated latency — immediate mitigations and follow-up

Logan / Laura — internal note and proposed short-term playbook for the VeloxAI incident (for the record):

Summary of root signals we've seen so far:
- A kernel scheduling regression on a subset of GPU instances combined with a hot-path KV-cache miss pattern for short context windows. The regression increases tail latency when many short sessions compete for the same compute slice.
- Client retries + immediate reconnects amplified inflight work and caused repeat token emissions in a few cases (replay/duplicate behavior).

Immediate technical actions taken (already done):
- Flipped routing to fallback model-variant on affected pool (conservative quantization settings) to smooth token cadence.
- Enabled prefix-KV caching TTL increase to 5m for the VeloxAI route.
- Applied a temporary per-route concurrency limit to avoid hot-slice saturation.

Recommended customer-facing guidance to send to VeloxAI right now:
1) Ask them to increase their streaming read timeout from 6s -> 12s for 1 hour while we monitor — reduces duplicate reconnects.
2) Recommend disabling aggressive client retry backoffs for 30–60 minutes.
3) Share the mitigation-checklist.pdf and the telemetry bundle (already attached in Logan's message).

Next steps for engineering:
- Infra to roll a micro-patch to kernel work-queue sizing (INC-2026-4123). ETA for patch: ~10 hours, will need a planned short maintenance window on affected pool.
- SRE to run a backfill job to re-synchronize KV caches for heavy prefixes.

I'll draft a short post-incident summary for the customer once we confirm stability.

— Marissa

Subject: Post-incident note — VeloxAI streaming behavior (Dec 5)

Hi Shelby —

Follow-up and summary after today's mitigation window. Thank you for the quick traces and for testing with our suggestions — that helped narrow the scope.

What we observed
- Window of impact: 08:40–09:05 PST. Root cause vector: combination of a kernel-level scheduling regression on a subset of GPU hosts plus amplified effect from client-side immediate reconnects. The regression increased tail latency under high short-session churn which produced the pause-then-burst behavior you saw.

What we did
- Customer-facing immediate mitigations: applied a conservative fallback model variant and raised prefix-KV TTLs, plus per-route concurrency limits. These reduced the pause frequency by ~85% in our post-change sampling.
- Engineering next steps: a micro-patch to the scheduler is tracked in INC-2026-4123; target deploy in a maintenance window tomorrow (Dec 6) with validation tests.

What you should do (recommended short-term client config)
- Increase streaming read timeout to 12s and avoid immediate client reconnects for 1–2 hours while the patch lands.
- If you observe duplicated messages, please capture the X-Session-Trace and send it to us; that will help us filter replays from duplicates for credits.

Make-good and follow-up
- We'll issue a one-time usage credit for affected token usage while mitigation was active (we'll calculate and propose the amount by end of day Monday).
- I propose a 30-minute technical sync tomorrow to walk through the micro-patch plan and validate VeloxAI's production configuration live. Please pick a time that works for your team: 09:30 PST or 14:30 PST.

Links and attachments:
- Incident ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026-4123
- Telemetry bundle (attached) and mitigation checklist.

Thanks again for your partnership and patience. We'll keep monitoring and will escalate immediately if anything unexpected appears.

Best,
